5.0.s.en: (1) The two prophets and the building of the temple

5.0.0.en: The people grew slack and no longer had enthusiasm for building the house of the Lord, for the following reasons:

5.0.1.en: 1- Their preoccupation with building their own private houses, and the rich among them cared for adorning them, so they paneled their houses on the inside (Hag 1:3).

5.0.2.en: 2- The weakness of their spiritual inclination. They had begun with enthusiasm, but their resolve weakened until it almost vanished with regard to building the house of the Lord.

5.0.3.en: Because of the severe spiritual weakness of the people, God sent them two prophets, not one prophet, Haggai and Zechariah, as He had sent earlier Elijah and Elisha, then Isaiah and after him Jeremiah, and likewise Daniel and Ezekiel in the captivity. The prophecy of Haggai began several months before the prophecy of Zechariah, and the prophecies of Haggai were marked by rebuke for the Jews' building of their own houses and their neglect of building the house of the Lord, while the prophecy of Zechariah was marked by encouragement (Zech 4:6). Thus by this complementarity the spiritual benefit is complete and the people rise up.

5.0.4.en: The prophecy of Haggai is also characterized by direct speech, whereas Zechariah uses visions abundantly to bring the meaning near.

5.0.5.en: The grace of God supported the two prophets, so they spoke in the name of the Lord, and they had awe and a spiritual influence on the people because of the Lord's support for them, especially since all the people were in slackness; even the two leaders, Zerubbabel and Jeshua, had yielded to this weakness. So it was necessary for God to intervene to encourage His people to worship Him.

5.1.0.en: The people responded to the words of the two prophets, and under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua began the building of the temple of God, whose building had stopped for about ten years.

5.1.1.en: The beginning of the building did not make the two prophets slack, but they continued in their work of encouragement and rebuke until the people completed the building of the temple, and perhaps they, together with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, shared with the people by their own hands in the building, to encourage the people.

5.1.2.en: The leaders of the work were the governor, who was Zerubbabel, the high priest, who was Jeshua, and the two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, and the leader of our spiritual life is Christ, the King, Priest and Prophet.

5.1.3.en: Zerubbabel is a type of Christ in the following:

5.1.4.en: 1- Zerubbabel brought the people of God back from captivity, and Christ freed us from the captivity of sin by His death on the Cross.

5.1.5.en: 2- Zerubbabel founded the new temple after the captivity, and Christ founded the temple of the Church of the New Testament by the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross, despite the opposition of enemies to both.

5.1.6.en: 3- Zerubbabel was of the tribe of Judah, and so was Christ.

5.2.0.en: The Persian Empire comprised twenty provinces, one of which was the province beyond the river, which includes the region lying west of the Euphrates river, that is, Syria, Palestine and the surrounding areas. The governor of this province was a man named Tatnai, and he was assisted in this province by Shethar-boznai. Complaints reached Tatnai from some of the surrounding nations that the Jews were building a temple without permission, or perhaps the inspectors under Tatnai throughout his province reported this building to him.

5.2.1.en: Tatnai and Shethar-boznai and a group of their assistants came to Jerusalem to verify the matter, and they found that the building of the temple was indeed under way. Tatnai spoke with the governor Zerubbabel, who was considered his subordinate over Jerusalem and Judea, and asked him and those with him about the permit they had to carry out this building. Tatnai's question was an inquiry so that matters would proceed properly, and not out of enmity or opposition, as had happened earlier with Rehum in (ch. 4).

5.3.0.en: Tatnai asked for the names of those carrying out the building, and Zerubbabel came forward boldly, wrote his name and the names of the chiefs who helped him in the building, and presented them to Tatnai. Here we see Tatnai's neutral integrity in keeping matters in order and knowing exactly what was going on in his province, and also the courage of Zerubbabel and all his helpers in the building, because God had encouraged them through the two prophets.

5.4.0.en: God gave the Jews favor in the eyes of Tatnai, so he did not stop them from completing the building of the temple, but told them that he would send to King Darius to verify their words, because Zerubbabel told him, as we shall see in the following verses, that Cyrus had issued an order to them to build. By the grace of God Tatnai tried to help them, so he paid no heed to the order of Artaxerxes to stop the building and promised them that he would inform them of Darius' reply on this matter. Here we see the accuracy of Ezra the priest and scribe, who was able to obtain the texts of the letters sent to the kings of Persia, whether from Rehum, who was hostile to the Jews, or from Tatnai, who was friendly to the Jews, and perhaps Ezra obtained these texts from the government records while he was living in captivity, before he came to Jerusalem.

5.4.1.en: God's eye is upon you, watching over you and supporting you, so do not be troubled by the opposition of enemies, but seek Him and rely on Him and continue in your spiritual striving, confident of His support.

5.5.0.en: Tatnai sent a letter to King Darius, giving him greetings at its beginning, as is the custom of letters, and it was signed by him and Shethar-boznai and the Apharsachites, who were a group of his assistants in the administration of the province.

5.6.0.en: Tatnai informed King Darius that he had visited Jerusalem to examine the information that had reached him, and saw for himself the building that was going on there. It is noticeable that in his report Tatnai tried to persuade the king and encourage him to agree to the completion of the building, and this appears from the following:

5.6.1.en: 1- He described the temple as the house of the great God. This means that God placed in Tatnai's heart reverence and fear of Him, for although he was a pagan who believed in many gods, he considered Him a great god among the gods.

5.6.2.en: 2- He magnified the building by describing it as being built with great stones, although they were the fallen stones left from the ruins of the temple of Solomon, and they were indeed huge stones (2 Chr 22:2), but he did not describe them as fallen stones, but as great.

5.6.3.en: 3- He declared to the king that the work was proceeding with speed and great success, to show the king the strength of the building and the blessing of this God who completes the building of His house and helps those who believe in Him.

5.6.4.en: The hand of God supports His children as long as they work faithfully and lovingly and in submission to His word, as the people submitted to the words of the two prophets. So be faithful in your work and service to God, and be sure that God will make you prosper and give you many blessings.

5.7.0.en: Tatnai informed Darius that when he examined what was being done in Jerusalem, he asked for the names of the chiefs responsible for the building, and wrote down all the names and sent them with this letter to the king, and this shows his accuracy and faithfulness; as he does his work faithfully, he also encourages the Jews. From Tatnai's question to the elders of Israel about who had commanded them to build the temple, it is understood that he had recently taken over the province beyond the river and did not know the order that had been issued by Cyrus in 536 BC, that is, sixteen years earlier.

5.8.0.en: Tatnai added that the elders of the Jews told him that they worship God, who is the God of heaven and earth. This is a magnification of God above the pagan gods, and although Tatnai says it on the tongue of the Jews, his informing Darius of it shows his esteem for God and for those who believe in Him.

5.8.1.en: The elders of the Jews also said that this house was built by a great king of theirs, meaning King Solomon, long ago, about 500 years before Darius, that is, about the year 1000 BC. This confirms the greatness of this house, that it was built by a great king and for a God who has no like, because He is the God of heaven and earth. The answer of the elders shows their courage and their faith in God when they said that He is the God of heaven and earth and were not afraid of the complaints of any of their enemies, because they had been strengthened by the word of God on the mouth of the two prophets.

5.9.0.en: The elders of the Jews confessed that they had sinned against their God and provoked Him to wrath, so He allowed Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to destroy this great house and take their fathers captive to the lands of the Babylonian kingdom. This is humility, repentance and acknowledgment of the truth on the part of the people of God.

5.10.0.en: The elders told Tatnai an important fact, which is that King Cyrus, the first of the kings of Persia, in the beginning of his reign, that is, in 538 BC, issued an order to rebuild this temple. That is, the order to build was issued from the beginning of the Persian Empire, and therefore the orders of kings are not repealed or turned back.

5.11.0.en: Tatnai added that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken the vessels of the house of the Lord, made of gold and silver, and carried them from Jerusalem to Babylon. After the fall of the Babylonian kingdom, Cyrus, the first of the kings of Media and Persia, became king and took these vessels from Babylon and gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, who is Zerubbabel, and made him governor of Jerusalem and Judea. Cyrus asked Sheshbazzar to build a house for the Lord in Jerusalem and to place these vessels in it.

5.11.1.en: From these two verses we see Tatnai's accuracy and his assurances that the Jews were building their temple by order of King Cyrus, and another proof of their truthfulness, that they had received the vessels of the house of their God from Cyrus, those which Nebuchadnezzar had seized and God had kept without harm until they returned to His house in Jerusalem. This also shows the power of God, who is able to preserve the vessels of His house and to move kings to carry out His will. We also find that Zerubbabel, that is, Sheshbazzar, is a person answerable before the Persian king; he does not act on his own, but holds a position dependent on the state and builds by order of the king. Thus Tatnai directs King Darius to the fact that Sheshbazzar, that is, Zerubbabel, is a person subject to the kingdom who carries out its orders and is not disobedient or rebellious, he and all who are with him, and this of course reassures the king and invites him to agree to and support the completion of the building of the temple.

5.12.0.en: Tatnai informed King Darius that Sheshbazzar had carried out the orders of King Cyrus and laid the foundation of the house of the Lord and was building in it, and the work on the building of the temple was still continuing. We notice in the words of Tatnai the following:

5.12.1.en: 1- Zerubbabel, that is, Sheshbazzar, is an obedient person committed to carrying out the orders of the king.

5.12.2.en: 2- He did not mention the period when the building was stopped, nor the complaints of Rehum and his companions, which continued for many years, nor how they stopped the building, so as not to confuse the king's mind, but considers that the building is proceeding in a natural way and only needs to be completed.

5.13.0.en: Tatnai concludes his letter with the following:

5.13.1.en: 1- A search for the order of Cyrus kept in the treasuries of the kingdom that are in Babylon, to confirm the truthfulness of the Jews, and this shows that Tatnai was a neutral and precise man.

5.13.2.en: 2- He did not ask King Darius to search for the complaints of Rehum or the order of Artaxerxes to stop the building, because he supports the Jews and wants their good and the building of their temple.

5.13.3.en: 3- Babylon was one of the capitals of the kingdom of Media and Persia, in addition to the city of Shushan the palace; that is, Babylon had been the capital of the Babylonian kingdom and continued as one of the capitals of the kingdom of Media and Persia.

5.13.4.en: 4- Tatnai declares his submission to King Darius and his waiting for his orders in this matter, so that he may carry it out. Darius and the completion of the house of the Lord

6.0.s.en: (1) The finding of the order of Cyrus

6.0.0.en: Darius gave attention to the letter of Tatnai and ordered a search for the order of King Cyrus for the building of the temple of the Lord, and his order was strict, so they took care to examine all the documents in the house of the rolls, which is a building in which the records of the kings of Persia and the various government orders are kept, and it was in the city of Babylon, which was one of the capitals of the Persian kingdom.

6.0.1.en: In Darius' conduct we see an attitude that helps the Jews and is not against them. He responded to the letter of Tatnai and searched for the evidence that would support the work of the Jews in completing the building, and of course this was because of God's work in his heart, as He worked long ago in the heart of Cyrus and made him command the building of the house of the Lord.

6.1.0.en: Achmetha: one of the capitals of the empire of Media and Persia, located in the region of Media and considered the summer resort of the kings, and called in Greek "Ecbatana."

6.1.1.en: The search for the order of Cyrus continued, and they did not find it in Babylon, and because Darius' order was strict, they searched also in the other capitals of the kingdom in which there were houses of the kings' records, so they went to Achmetha and searched carefully, and finally found this order of Cyrus. The finding of the order means a number of things:

6.1.2.en: 1- The care of Darius and his assistants in searching everywhere for the order of Cyrus, because he was sympathetic to the Jews and wanted to support them in this matter, so he was not content with its not being found in Babylon and order the building to be stopped, but the search continued until they found it.

6.1.3.en: 2- God's care in preserving this document after sixteen years, during which the document could have been lost or damaged.

6.1.4.en: 3- The search continuing for a long time allowed the Jews to continue building the temple, and this was a grace from God to them.

6.2.0.en: The assistants of Darius found the order of King Cyrus, and it contained the following:

6.2.1.en: 1- It was issued in the first year of Cyrus' reign.

6.2.2.en: 2- It concerns the building of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.

6.2.3.en: 3- It is to be built in the place of the old house of the Lord which was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar.

6.2.4.en: 4- He allowed its dimensions to be sixty cubits in length and likewise sixty cubits in breadth, that is, that it should not exceed these dimensions, or should be within them, and he allows the Jews to build the house with the measurements they want, especially since the measurements of the temple of Solomon were less than what Cyrus allowed.

6.2.5.en: 5- He allowed it not to exceed these dimensions, or to be within the limits of these dimensions, and he allows the Jews to build the house with the measurements they want, especially since the measurements of the temple of Solomon were less than what Cyrus allowed.

6.2.6.en: 6- He specified the building materials, which were great stones and new timber, and this shows the care of King Cyrus for the building of a house of greater standing, and at the same time it supports the Jews who were building with great stones, as Tatnai saw and explained in his letter to Darius, that they were carrying out the order of Cyrus and were doing nothing for which anyone could call them to account.

6.2.7.en: 7- He also specified the manner of building, which was to build the stones in three rows, then a row of timber, and so on, that is, repeating this throughout the building, so that it would be strong and firmly bonded.

6.2.8.en: 8- The funding of the building of the house of the Lord was to be at the king's expense.

6.2.9.en: 9- The return of the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, so that these vessels would be returned to Jerusalem and placed in the house of the Lord for its service.

6.2.10.en: Now in this chapter we see that the details of the order of Cyrus the great king, which were not mentioned before, show the extent of his sympathy and care for the building of the house of the Lord, such as the dimensions of the house, the type of building materials and the manner of building.

6.2.11.en: God is ready to support you with many proofs and helps if your heart believes in Him and relies on Him and you do His will. He is with you and defends you in all that you do.

6.3.0.en: After Satan's attempts to stop the building of the house of the Lord, from the days of Rehum and King Artaxerxes (Cambyses) until the days of Darius, God intervenes and makes Darius sympathetic to the Jews, because "the king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will" (Prov 2:1). Darius issued an order for the building of the house of the Lord to continue, in which the following appeared:

6.3.1.en: 1- He respected the order of the former king Cyrus, because some kings in pride neglect the orders of former kings, and even oppose them.

6.3.2.en: 2- His order to Tatnai was definite and firm that the building should not be hindered, so all the soldiers and assistants of Tatnai were to keep away and not hinder the Jews from completing the temple of their God.

6.3.3.en: 3- He commanded Zerubbabel the governor of the Jews and their elders to complete the house of the Lord.

6.3.4.en: 4- The wisdom of Darius appears in his concern to win the love of his subjects, for permitting the Jews to build the temple of their God makes them loyal and submissive to him.

6.4.0.en: After the first item of Darius' order, the continuation of the building, the second item in this verse was the spending on this building from the money of the kingdom, so he commanded the governor beyond the river, who was Zerubbabel's superior, to give him money from the tribute collected on behalf of the king, so that Zerubbabel could complete the building. This shows Darius' great sympathy with the Jews and his awareness of their circumstances, since they were poor and needed financial help, and in this he followed the example of Cyrus the Great, who commanded that the building of the house of the Lord be paid for from the money of the kingdom.

6.5.0.en: The third item of Darius' order is his request to Tatnai to give the Jews their needs of the animals offered as burnt offerings in the temple, as well as the foodstuffs that accompany these burnt offerings when they are offered to God, such as wheat and wine... in the quantities the priests ask for according to the needs of the temple. This shows great concern on the part of Darius that the burnt offerings should continue to be offered before God, so that he says that it be given them "day by day without fail", that is, that the offering of these sacrifices should never stop.

6.5.1.en: The fourth item in Darius' order is his request to the Jews to pray always before God for him and his sons. It is useful to know about Darius that he believed in the idea of one God but did not know Him, so he agreed with the Jews in their belief in one God, since he hated the multiplicity of gods and the worship of idols. Although he did not yet believe in God, he was comforted by, and greatly esteemed, the Jews' worship of one God, so he sympathized with them greatly, as appears from this order of his.

6.6.0.en: The fifth item in Darius' order is the punishment of everyone who tries to hinder the building of the temple, and he fixed the punishment, which is very severe: that a beam be pulled out of those with which his house was built, and consequently his house would be torn down and become wreckage, ruins and a dunghill on which people's filth is thrown, and then he would be hanged on this beam, that is, the destruction of this man, the demolition of his house and the scattering of his family.

6.6.1.en: Whoever tries to fortify himself in his firm, settled house and stops the building of the house of the Lord, his house is demolished and he perishes in a horrible way, which is hanging with an instrument from his own house, while the house of the Lord is built and completed, so that his evil comes upon his own head and he perishes, but the house of God is completed.

6.7.0.en: In the end Darius showed his faith in God as a great God, able to punish His enemies, in his prayer to Him to destroy every king or people that opposes Him.

6.7.1.en: At the end of the letter containing this order, Darius signed it and commanded that this order be carried out with speed.

6.7.2.en: From this we see a miraculous divine work that took place in the heart of Darius, so that he gave this order, which contains the speedy carrying out of the following:

6.7.3.en: 1- Not hindering the building of the temple and continuing to build it.

6.7.4.en: 2- Spending on the needs of the temple from the money of the state.

6.7.5.en: 3- Providing the animals and foodstuffs that must be offered to God in His temple.

6.7.6.en: 4- Asking for prayer on his behalf and on behalf of his sons.

6.7.7.en: 5- Punishing whoever opposes the building of the temple with death by hanging, the demolition of his house and its turning into a dunghill. In the order of Darius we see how God turns evil into good: if Satan stirred up the wicked against the house of the Lord, yet God, who is stronger than he, when His people drew near to Him, moved Darius, and he gave an order better and stronger than the order of Cyrus.

6.7.8.en: Do not fear the wars of the devil, but take refuge in God and ask for all you need, and He will intervene quickly and give you more than you ask or think.

6.8.s.en: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

6.8.0.en: Tatnai rejoiced at the order of Darius, which came in agreement with Tatnai's feelings, and he hastened to carry out the order with all exactness. This confirms the faithfulness of Tatnai, who had first sent precisely all that he had seen in the building of the house of the Lord, and here he now hastens to carry out the orders of the king. All this was by the providence of God in completing the building of His house.

6.9.0.en: The Jews were encouraged, so they worked quickly to complete the building, until the building of the house of the Lord was finished, and they fulfilled the word of God that He spoke on the mouth of His two prophets Haggai and Zechariah, that Zerubbabel would complete the building (Hag 1:8, Zech 4:9). In this they pleased God and also obeyed the kings of Persia, namely Cyrus and Darius and also Artaxerxes, who reigned later and in whose days Ezra and Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem, where they built the wall of the city. Ezra here, the writer of the book, mentions all the kings of Persia who encouraged and commanded the Jews to take care of building the house of the Lord and the wall of His city. The Artaxerxes mentioned here did not share in building the temple, but was mentioned in his honor, because after more than seventy years from the building of the temple he commanded the building of the wall of Jerusalem.

6.10.0.en: The completion of the building of the temple began in the second year of Darius' reign (Ezra 3:8) and the building was finished in the sixth year of his reign, that is, it took about four years, and that was in 516 BC, on the third day of the month of Adar in the Syriac calendar, which corresponds to the month of March in the Gregorian year.

6.11.0.en: The priests, the Levites and the rest of the people gathered to dedicate the house of the Lord, that it might become a holy place for the worship of God, and it was a great day on which they expressed their love for God by offering a large number of sacrifices: a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, in addition to twelve he-goats. We notice in these sacrifices the following:

6.11.1.en: 1- Their number was much less than what Solomon offered at the dedication of the temple, and also what King Hezekiah and King Josiah offered in the celebration of the Passover (1 Kgs 8:63; 2 Chr 30:24; 35:7).

6.11.2.en: 2- They offered sin offerings because they had sinned by neglecting the building of the house of the Lord, but at the building of the altar and the founding of the temple they offered only burnt offerings to please God.

6.11.3.en: 3- They offered twelve he-goats for the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, although those returning from captivity were of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. This shows that those returning had become the one kingdom of Israel, offering sin offerings in love for their brethren, whether few of these tribes had returned, or some of them might return in time.

6.11.4.en: All the people rejoiced, great and small, men, women and children, at the satisfaction of God with them, because He had brought them back from captivity and granted them to build His house. But God here called them the children of the captivity, so that they would always remember their sin, because of which they were taken captive, but the mercy of God brought them back from the captivity.

6.11.5.en: We see clearly that the house of the Lord that Zerubbabel built was much less than the one that Solomon built, and here is this comparison between the two houses:

6.11.6.en: Table comparing the temple of Solomon and the temple of Zerubbabel. No. Type of comparison, Temple of Solomon, Temple of Zerubbabel. 1 Duration of its building: seven continuous years, 9 years, of which only six months was building in (1 Kgs 6:38) the reign of Cyrus, then the building stopped for four and a half years, then the building was completed in four years in the reign of Darius (Ezra 6:15). 2 Its equipment: David prepared most of it; the ruins of the temple of Solomon + the people's contributions + the gifts of the Persian state. 3 Its appearance: splendid in its beauty and greatness; very modest compared with the temple of Solomon (Hag 2:3). 4 God's coming: at its a thick cloud prevented the priests from no material form of God's coming appeared.

6.11.7.en: dedication, standing in the temple (1 Kgs 8:11). 5 The ark of the covenant: they brought it up to the temple with great glory; the presence of an ark of the covenant is not mentioned in this (1 Kgs 8:5). temple, because it was most likely lost.

6.11.8.en: 6 Dedication sacrifices: 22 thousand bulls and 120 thousand sheep; 100 bulls and 200 rams and 400 lambs. 7 The kingdom: one strong kingdom comprising the twelve tribes; one weak kingdom comprising the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and it was a province subject to the Persian kingdom. 8 The king: the greatest king in his time; there was no king, rather Israel was a province of Solomon subject to the Persian kingdom. 9 Its glory: great in its appearance; despite its modesty it was greater than the temple of Solomon because Christ entered it (Hag 2:9).

6.12.0.en: After the dedication of the temple they organized the service in it, by arranging the divisions of the priests and the divisions of the Levites, who took turns in the service, that is, life and worship returned to the house of the Lord.

6.13.0.en: The people rejoiced in the temple of God and kept their most important feast, the Passover, on the fourteenth day of the first month, after they had kept the lamb for fourteen days as the Law prescribed (Ex 12:1-10). In this every family showed its thanks to God, who freed them from the bondage of Babylon by the orders of Cyrus, then the support of Darius, as they thanked God long ago by keeping the Passover in Egypt, when He preserved their firstborn and struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues, then released them to worship Him in the wilderness of Sinai.

6.13.1.en: It is mentioned in the Old Testament that the children of Israel kept the Passover six times, which are:

6.13.2.en: 1- In the land of Egypt in the days of Moses, immediately before their exodus (Ex 12:1-11).

6.13.3.en: 2- In the wilderness of Sinai in the days of Moses (Num 5:9).

6.13.4.en: 3- In Gilgal in the days of Joshua (Josh 5:10).

6.13.5.en: 4- In the days of King Hezekiah (2 Chr 30:15).

6.13.6.en: 5- In the time of King Josiah (2 Kgs 23:21).

6.13.7.en: 6- In the days of Zerubbabel (Ezra 6:19). This does not mean that the Passover was not kept except these six times, but these times are mentioned because they carry a covenant with God and a renewal of the relationship with Him.

6.14.0.en: The priests and the Levites took care to prepare for the Passover, so they purified themselves according to the Law, and consequently carried out their role in slaughtering the Passover lambs for every family of the children of Israel, and all kept the feast to the Lord.

6.15.0.en: In this Passover there shared the Jews returning from captivity, in addition to the Jews who had been living in the land of Israel and had not gone into captivity and had mingled through pagan marriages; they separated themselves from them and purified themselves, so they were able to eat of the Passover.

6.15.1.en: The purpose of keeping the Passover here becomes clear: that they sought God, that is, they returned to Him with their hearts, leaving what they had learned in captivity from the pagans, and appeared as a people who believe in God.

6.16.0.en: They completed the Feast of the Passover by keeping the Feast of Unleavened Bread that follows it for seven days, and they rejoiced in their worship of God who brought them back from captivity by the hand of Cyrus, and they built the house of the Lord by the order of Cyrus and Darius, who reigned over all the lands that had been subject to Assyria and Babylon. If Assyria had taken them captive long ago, now the one who reigns over Assyria, that is, Cyrus, then Darius, bring them back and build for them the temple of their God.

6.16.1.en: With the end of this chapter Ezra concludes the account of a period of time that began in 536 BC with the return of the people of God under Zerubbabel and continued until 516 BC (chs. 1-6), when the house of the Lord was built and dedicated, a period of thirty years.

6.16.2.en: Your true joy is in your worship of God in His Church and in your closet. So take care to give the best times of your life, to enjoy being in the presence of God, so that you let Him into your life and He works in you with power. Ezra and the second return to Jerusalem

6.16.3.en: 1- The events mentioned in (chs. 1-6) took thirty years, from 536 to 516 BC, as we mentioned, and in this period important figures appeared, namely Zerubbabel the civil governor, Jeshua the high priest, and the two prophets Haggai and Zechariah. Then a period of 58 years passed in which Persian kings reigned, among whom we know Ahasuerus, who reigned from 486 to 465 BC, and during whose reign the events of the Book of Esther took place and the book was written during this period.

6.16.4.en: 2- In the year 458 begin the events mentioned in this book from (chs. 7-10), and we see in them the second return from captivity under Ezra the priest and scribe, accompanied by 1,700 men, that is, about 8,000 persons of men, women and children. The book here mentions the details of the works of the great Ezra in Jerusalem.

6.16.5.en: 3- Ezra was a contemporary of Nehemiah, who led the third return to Jerusalem in 445 BC, that is, thirteen years later, and remained governor of Jerusalem and its surroundings for about 12-13 years, and Ezra and Nehemiah were contemporaries of the prophet Malachi, who prophesied about 433 BC. The second return was in the time of King Artaxerxes, called Longimanus, who was the son of King Ahasuerus, the husband of Esther.
